item.title: Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements
item.description: arXiv:2611.16750v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Machine learning coupled with device simulation is widely used to optimize thin-film solar cells, but almost exclusively in the forward direction, from device parameters to predicted performance. The inverse problem encountered after fabrication, namely identifying the mechanism that limits a given device, is still addressed by manual inspection of characterization data. In this work, both directions are examined for lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells using approximately 42,000 SCAPS-1D simulations. Replacing the Spiro-OMeTAD hole transport layer with CuI increases the simulated power conversion efficiency from 19.6\% to 21.6\%, almost entirely through the fill factor. Surrogate models trained and tested on a factorial parameter grid substantially overstate their predictive accuracy. An XGBoost regressor attains $R^2 = 0.9997$ on held-out grid points but only 0.58 on independently sampled devices, whereas training on a Latin hypercube design of comparable size restores $R^2 = 0.995$. For the inverse problem, a multi-label classifier identifies which of six degradation mechanisms are present from simulated temperature- and illumination-dependent open-circuit-voltage measurements. It achieves a macro $F_1$ score of 0.938, compared to 0.687 for a calibrated physics-rule baseline. The classifier does not, however, generalize to combinations of mechanisms absent from the training set.
item.dc:creator: Nabanita Sarker, Hafiz Imtiaz

item.title: Finite cyclic monodromy in BMS3 gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.16823v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate inducing data for three dimensional asymptotically flat BMS gravity on hyperbolic Virasoro orbits with winding, which contain no constant supermomentum, and the restriction of formal smooth equivariant sections to global Lorentz orbits. Using the developing map of the associated Hill operator we rederive their stabilizer and show that, in the spin double cover, it is the direct product of a line with a cyclic group of even order. The character of the cyclic factor is therefore a discrete inducing label independent of the continuous one, unlike for the massive BMS particles, where it is fixed by the spin. At points with the corresponding finite rotational symmetry, restriction of formal smooth equivariant sections to a global Lorentz orbit yields the finite cyclic equivariance condition, while an independently defined unitary global branch realizes the associated finite difference equation. At points with timelike projected momentum we derive the resulting ladder of Poincare helicities, show that the projected rest energy is not an orbit invariant, construct locally flat winding BMS geometries with hyperbolic Lorentz holonomy, prove that the smooth real periodic near horizon current model excludes these winding orbits, and obtain selection rules and closed form expressions for finite monodromy resolved orbital functionals. A unitary realization on the full infinite dimensional orbit is not constructed, and the interpretation of the cyclic sectors in quantum gravity remains conjectural.
item.dc:creator: Evangelos Melas

item.title: The uniqueness of smooth stationary black holes
item.description: arXiv:2611.16853v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the domain of outer communications of a smooth, asymptotically flat, stationary vacuum spacetime describing a single rotating non-degenerate black hole is isometric to the domain of outer communications of a subextremal Kerr solution under reasonable geometric and physical assumptions, without analyticity or any smallness assumptions. The method is to apply Harrison transform to construct a family of solutions of Einstein--Maxwell equations. Combining null area comparison with the area-charge inequality, we show that, in the limiting transformed geometry, the bifurcate sphere has area radius one and constant electric and magnetic flux densities, with the original ADM mass normalized to $M=1$. These identities imply the technical assumptions of Ionescu--Klainerman, yielding the identification with Kerr.
item.dc:creator: Yishen Huang, Jiongyue Li, Junbin Li, Xi-Ping Zhu

item.title: An FBSDE Approach to the Two-Dimensional Abelian-Higgs Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.16875v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop an iterated forward-backward stochastic differential equation (FBSDE) approach to the two-dimensional infinite-volume Abelian-Higgs model in Coulomb gauge. We prove tightness of the joint renormalized lattice gauge-Higgs laws, after continuum extension, as the lattice spacing tends to zero and the volume tends to infinity. We represent the lattice measure as the joint terminal law of the FBSDEs and establish uniform moment bounds for the corresponding terminal shifts. For the Higgs field, we combine a low-high frequency decomposition with covariant energy estimates to obtain bounds with sufficiently mild dependence on the gauge shift. For the gauge field, we establish high-frequency estimates for the effective force and combine them with quantitative diamagnetic control in the infrared.
item.dc:creator: Zexi He

item.title: Braided module categories from small braidings
item.description: arXiv:2611.16900v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce small braidings on inclusions of monoidal categories $\mathcal{C}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{D}$, which allow one to braid objects in $\mathcal{C}$ with objects in $\mathcal{D}$. A small braiding makes $\mathcal{C}$ a braided monoidal category, and turns $\mathcal{D}$, as well as certain subcategories of $\mathcal{D}$, into braided module categories over $\mathcal{C}$. We prove versions of previously known reconstruction results for braided module categories which do not rely on finiteness assumptions. We construct a number of new examples coming from quantum groups, as well as the associated quantum moment maps.
item.dc:creator: Tyler Franke, Ingo Runkel, Volker Schomerus

item.title: When can local unitaries generate a complete orthogonal basis?
item.description: arXiv:2611.16921v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The question of local encodability asks: can a given, multipartite pure quantum state be completed to an orthonormal basis using only local unitary rotations? If any such state in a given system has this property, it is called universally locally encodable (ULE), a feature, which has applications in quantum information theory, engineering and math. Despite its easy formulation, the answer to this question depends nontrivially on the local dimensions of the system: While universal local encodability is known for $2\times 2$, $4\times 4$ and $8\times 8$-dimensional systems, it was so-far only conjectured to hold in $3\times 3$, and non-ULE was recently proved for systems of four and more qubits by Pauwels and G\"uhne. We resolve the open conjecture by proving universality for two qutrits. Furthermore, we construct (among others) universal local encodings in dimensions $d\times2$ for $d\ge2$, in dimensions $d\times3$ for $d=3,4$ and $d\ge6$, and in every bipartite system with one or two infinite-dimensional subsystems. For finite-dimensional multipartite systems, we turn a heuristic parameter count into a necessary condition for universality, which excludes universal local encodability in infinitely many cases. Finally, we give universal local encodability an operational interpretation by showing that non-ULE is equivalent to whether general measurements yield an advantage over projectively simulable ones in discrimination tasks where unknown, random local unitary rotations have to be detected.
item.dc:creator: Julian Eisfeld, Hermann Kampermann, Nikolai Wyderka

item.title: GFF for 3D Ising interfaces in three moves of Tetris
item.description: arXiv:2611.16943v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that at sufficiently large inverse-temperature $\beta>0$, the 3D Ising model on the torus, under boundary conditions that have a positive slope $\theta_1,\theta_2>0$, has a GFF scaling limit for its interface. The proof goes through three steps of a Tetris map, which lets cubes drop according to gravity in each of the three axes, yielding Solid-On-Solid (SOS), Half-Monotone SOS (HMSOS) and monotone surfaces (dimers). We establish GFF limits sequentially, in particular resolving the analogous problem for the $(2+1)$D SOS. A crucial ingredient is an improved RG analysis for interacting dimers, which is of independent interest: it relaxes the assumptions on interactions from being uniformly bounded in $L^\infty$ to only being typically small.
item.dc:creator: Beno\^{\i}t Laslier, Eyal Lubetzky

item.title: Off-diagonal decay of capacitance matrices via Brownian motion
item.description: arXiv:2611.16978v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish upper and lower bounds for the off-diagonal entries of the capacitance matrix of infinite systems of spherical resonators in chain, screen and crystal geometries. Let $d$ denote the distance between two resonator centres. For chains contained in a cylinder of bounded radius and with bounded axial gaps, the decay is of order $d^{-1}\log^{-2}(2+d)$. For screens contained in a slab and relatively dense in the tangential directions, it is of order $d^{-3}$. For relatively dense three-dimensional configurations, we obtain exponential upper and lower bounds. No periodicity is assumed. Our proofs are based on the classical connection between the Dirichlet problem and Brownian motion, which enables us to relate the decay estimates to hitting probabilities of Brownian motion.
item.dc:creator: Habib Ammari, Clemens Thalhammer

item.title: How to arrange four points in the plane
item.description: arXiv:2611.16990v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Arranging points in the plane appears to be an elementary geometric problem, yet it is deeply rooted in statistical physics. As a toy model, we consider the configuration of four points. We completely classify the minimal configurations of four points interaction energy in $\R^2$ under the general Lennard-Jones potentials $V(r)=r^{-p}-br^{-q}$, where $p>q>0$ and $b\in\R$. We find that there is a threshold curve \[ D_{p,q}=2^{-(p-q)/2}\Bigl(1+\frac{p-q}{q+2}\bigl(1+2^{-(q+2)/2}\bigr)\Bigr) \] to determine the minimal shapes. The main results can be stated concisely as follows: consider $\min\sum_{1\le i<j\le4}\bigl(|x_i-x_j|^{-p}-b|x_i-x_j|^{-q}\bigr)$. For $b\le0$, the minimizer does not exist. For $b>0$, the minimizer is unique up to rotation and translation. Furthermore, the minimizer is \[ \begin{cases} \text{a square},&\hbox{if}\;\; D_{p,q}\ge1, \text{a rhombus with angle }\theta\in(\pi/3,\pi/2),&\hbox{if}\;\; D_{p,q}<1. \end{cases} \]
item.dc:creator: Senping Luo

item.title: Infinite spin superparticles
item.description: arXiv:2611.17006v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We obtain infinite spin representations of the super-Poincar\'e algebra from a higher-derivative superparticle action on a super-Minkowski background in 3, 4, 6 and 10 dimensions. Super-twistor transforms are performed, and used to deduce first-quantised spectra.
item.dc:creator: Eugenia Boffo, Martin Cederwall

item.title: Irreversible dynamics for ideal fluids on Riemannian manifolds: metriplectic energy-conserving alternatives to Navier-Stokes
item.description: arXiv:2611.17049v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For modelling dissipative phenomena such as friction, diffusion and viscosity, the Hamiltonian framework has a key limitation: once the Casimir invariants are fixed, Hamiltonian flows preserve phase-space volume, which rules out relaxation to equilibrium. Thus modelling dissipation requires modifying the Hamiltonian structure. Following the metriplectic (equivalently, GENERIC) approach, we add to the Hamiltonian vector field a dissipative term generated by a symmetric bracket, here constructed from a Riemannian metric. The resulting flow conserves the energy, and optionally further invariants, while driving a chosen generalised entropy monotonically, which makes the dynamics irreversible; when the entropy is bounded on energy level sets in the direction in which it is driven, it acts as a Lyapunov functional. We apply this construction to ideal fluids on compact Riemannian manifolds, choosing Casimirs of the Lie-Poisson bracket as entropies. In two dimensions, dissipating enstrophy yields the already-known energy-constrained Navier-Stokes equations, which include a nonlocal term restoring energy balance. In three dimensions, where enstrophy is no longer a Casimir, we derive new irreversible models. For incompressible and compressible fluids carrying an advected scalar, dissipating potential enstrophy or higher potential-vorticity moments gives a nonlinear, anisotropic diffusion that acts to align the gradients of the scalar and of the potential vorticity. For a purely incompressible fluid, taking helicity as the entropy gives a first-order, non-smoothing dissipative term whose stationary states are Beltrami fields.
item.dc:creator: Erwin Luesink, Archishman Saha, Tanya Schmah, Cristina Stoica

item.title: Mass gap for the fractional $\Phi^4_2$ model
item.description: arXiv:2611.17119v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a new, simple and self-contained technique for proving a mass gap for Euclidean quantum field theories in the high-temperature regime using the stochastic quantisation approach. As an application, we establish exponential decay of spatial correlations for the fractional $\Phi^4$ model on the plane in the Wick-ordering regime. The key idea is to analyse the propagation of perturbations using the linearised stochastic quantisation equation. Spatial propagation is controlled by an auxiliary random walk, while the potentially destabilising effect of the renormalised nonlinearity is controlled by combining dissipative energy estimates for the nonlinear dynamic with the Bou\'e-Dupuis variational formula.
item.dc:creator: Pawe{\l} Duch, Massimiliano Gubinelli

item.title: Exact characterization of three-terminal fermion counting under one-body scattering
item.description: arXiv:2611.17122v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum scattering is a fundamental probe of the scattering region and the quantum dynamics of outgoing particles. In two terminals, the statistics of non-interacting fermions is described by a generalized binomial distribution, that arises from the Pauli exclusion principle, while deviations are a signature of interactions. In this work, we extend this result to a scattering region coupled to three outgoing terminals (or channels), obtaining exact bounds for the statistics of the outgoing fermions. In particular, for two fermions and three terminals, four inequalities involving six measured probabilities determine whether a non-interacting scatterer can explain the observed statistics. Applying these inequalities to recent scattering experiments in cold atoms, we are able to identify a regime where interactions have a significant contribution on the outgoing particles. Therefore, our work opens up the possibility of identifying fermion interactions at the nanoscale in systems that range from mesoscopic conductors to optical traps in cold atoms.
item.dc:creator: Zhanning Wang, Yongtao Li, Rub\'en Seoane Souto, Jos\'e C. Abadillo-Uriel

item.title: ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs
item.description: arXiv:2611.17141v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A foundational principle of physics is that all coordinate systems are equally valid: the behavior of a PDE-governed system does not depend on the origin or orientation of the frame, nor on the units or mesh used to write it down, and neither should a surrogate model. Yet the neural surrogates with the lowest errors on today's aerodynamics benchmarks lack these invariances and fail under simple transformations of the same problem: for models trained on PDEs of cars in one pose (i.e., translation and rotation) and from one mesher, rotating the full PDE raises the surface-pressure error from 4% to more than 100%, and re-sampling its boundary raises it to about 30%. We introduce ISLA (Invariant Slice Attention), a slice-attention transformer for steady, boundary-driven PDEs in which no learned operation receives a coordinate and every sum over the boundary is a quadrature. Positions enter only as distances and relative angles to learned slice anchors, lengths are measured in a unit computed from the boundary, and interior points query the boundary through a tree-accelerated learned kernel without influencing one another. With every boundary cell a token and an exact boundary read, ISLA is equivariant to rigid motions and reflections, invariant to the units of its declared data, and consistent under mesh refinement, while at every setting each query is independent of all other queries. On AeroZoo, 2,816 flows that vary in shape, size, speed, and boundary conditions, its mean reference-scaled velocity and pressure errors are at least 3.1 and 3.3 times lower than any baseline's. On AirfRANS its errors are second only to those of a boundary-integral model (GLOBE) and at least 1.6 times lower than those of Transolver and GeoTransolver.
item.dc:creator: Peter Sharpe

item.title: Radius decay and boundary polymers: cluster expansion for long-range many-body tilts
item.description: arXiv:2611.17193v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider a nearest-neighbor Gibbs measure on a region in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ (e.g., the Ising model) tilted by $\sum_{x,r} g_{x,r}$, where $g_{x,r}$ is an arbitrary function of the spins in the ball of radius $r$ about $x$, with $\|g_{x,r}\|_\infty\leq \exp(-C r)$: an exponential decay in the radius of the ball rather than in its volume. Standard cluster expansions fail for such many-body tilts, as a ball of radius $r$ carries $\exp(c r^2)$ configurations. We show that the partition function can be resummed into a polymer model whose polymers are outer boundaries of connected unions of balls, decorated by the spins along them, with weights decaying exponentially in the boundary length. The proof uses only the domain Markov property of the base measure; it develops a version of this resummation argument that appeared in a recent work of the authors in the context of RG analysis of Grassmann variables. As applications, we show convergent cluster expansions for many-body tilts of Ising models at high and low temperatures; existence of infinite-volume limits; and exponential decay of correlations.
item.dc:creator: Beno\^{\i}t Laslier, Eyal Lubetzky

item.title: Higher Categorical Bistellar Moves
item.description: arXiv:2611.17244v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct $n$-categories $\mathscr{P}_n$ with generators given by simplices and relations given by bistellar moves between them, in any dimension $n$. We show that functors out of $\mathscr{P}_n$ into an $n$-category of theories, give the correct input for the orbifold construction for TQFTs, and subsume all previously known examples, which are all in dimensions $n \leq 3$. In particular, in dimension 3 the construction gives a highly nontrivial categorification of a kind of nonunital, noncounital, Frobenius algebra.
item.dc:creator: Aleksandar Ivanov

item.title: Structure-Preserving Integrators for Locally Conformally Symplectic Systems: Variational Methods and Globalization
item.description: arXiv:2611.17256v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Locally conformally symplectic (LCS) manifolds are characterized by a nondegenerate two-form $\Omega$ satisfying $\mathrm{d}\Omega=\varphi\wedge\Omega$, where $\varphi$ is a closed one-form, called the Lee form. Although an LCS structure is locally conformal to an ordinary symplectic structure, the local symplectic descriptions need not arise from a single global symplectic form. This creates a natural local-to-global problem for geometric numerical integration: local symplectic discretizations must be compatible on chart overlaps in order to determine a globally defined numerical dynamics. We develop a Hamiltonian variational framework for the construction and globalization of structure-preserving integrators for LCS systems. The continuous theory is first recalled in a form adapted to a Type~II Hamiltonian variational principle. We then introduce exact and approximate discrete right Hamiltonians for the local symplectic representatives and identify the transformation law that they must satisfy on overlaps. This compatibility condition implies equivariance of the associated local discrete Hamiltonian maps and therefore provides a sufficient condition for their globalization. The resulting global discrete map preserves the LCS two-form conformally, with a discrete conformal factor determined by the local conformal potentials. The framework applies naturally to Type~II Hamiltonian variational integrators and, in the cotangent-type setting considered here, to symplectic Runge--Kutta methods. In particular, Gauss--Legendre methods and the implicit midpoint rule yield globally compatible LCS structure-preserving schemes. Under suitable regularity assumptions, the corresponding Lagrangian formulation is recovered through discrete Legendre transformations. Numerical examples illustrate overlap compatibility, chart switching, convergence, and discrete conformal preservation.
item.dc:creator: Ayten Gezici, Melvin Leok, Cristina Sard\'on

item.title: Twisting IKKT with branes
item.description: arXiv:2611.17270v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by the conjectural relationship between the IKKT matrix model and type IIB string theory, we classify supersymmetric twists of the matrix model, allowing for both dynamical and kinematical supercharges. Beyond the two twists available at any finite $N$, which we studied in our previous work, we find five additional classes at infinite rank which require non-commuting backgrounds associated with D-branes in IIB supergravity. Together, these twists realize representatives of every equivalence class of twisting supercharges in flat-space type IIB supergravity recently classified by the first author; however, the precise form of the orbit stratification differs. This difference is related to a higher central extension of the IIB superalgebra that appears in our treatment of the IKKT model in the BV formalism. Expanding around the non-commutative backgrounds gives worldvolume theories on products of A- and B-branes, including four-dimensional BF theory on an emergent D3-brane. We relate all these twists to deformations of BCOV theory (the closed string field theory of the topological B-model) using the open-closed duality of classical string field theory. For one of the twists with Spin$(7)$ symmetry, we also show the localization of the IKKT partition function by Moore, Nekrasov, and Shatashvili can be directly reconstructed with the BV formalism, with their auxiliary field completion encoded by quadratic antifield terms. Throughout, we provide self-contained treatments of the formal techniques we employ.
item.dc:creator: Fabian Hahner, Natalie M. Paquette

item.title: Near-Optimal Multiparameter Pure-State Metrology with a Constant Number of Bases
item.description: arXiv:2611.17281v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multiparameter pure-state metrology is limited by the incompatibility of measurements optimized for different parameters. We characterize uniform sensitivity by the Fisher floor, the smallest fraction of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) retained over all pure states and parameter directions. We prove that a constant number of fixed orthonormal bases suffices for a nearly optimal Fisher floor, independently of the Hilbert-space dimension $d$. With high probability, five independent Haar bases already achieve a positive, dimension-independent floor, and larger constant families achieve approximate universal Fisher symmetry: they retain nearly one half of the QFI in every direction, the largest uniform fraction permitted by measurement incompatibility. The required number of bases is optimal up to a logarithmic factor in inverse accuracy. In contrast, $d+1$ mutually unbiased bases, when they exist, can minimize mean Fisher anisotropy among families of $d+1$ bases yet have a Fisher floor of at most $1/(d+1)$, showing that optimal average balance does not ensure uniform sensitivity.
item.dc:creator: Bowen Xiao, Zhiyao Yang, Huangjun Zhu

item.title: Quantum Metrology and Quantum Battery in a Hyperfine-Coupled Spin System
item.description: arXiv:2611.17310v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate multiparameter quantum metrology and the energetic properties of an effective electron--proton spin system inspired by the hyperfine structure of the hydrogen atom. Considering the external magnetic field $\mathcal B$ and the hyperfine coupling strength $\Lambda$ as unknown parameters, we derive the quantum Fisher information matrix and establish the corresponding quantum Cram\'er--Rao bounds for their simultaneous estimation. We analyze the estimation precision and the correlations between the two parameters, showing that the weak-commutativity condition is satisfied despite the noncommutativity of the associated symmetric logarithmic derivatives. Independently, we explore the energetic properties of the system under a unitary charging protocol, characterizing its ergotropy, anti-ergotropy, storage capacity, and energy-basis coherence. We investigate the dependence of these quantities on the magnetic field, hyperfine coupling, temperature, and charging time. Our results provide a comprehensive characterization of the metrological properties and energetic performance of a hyperfine spin-based quantum system, highlighting its potential as a platform for quantum sensing and energy storage.
item.dc:creator: Omar Bachain, Mohamed Amazioug, Rachid Ahl Laamara

item.title: Macroscopic diffusive fluctuations for generalized hard rods dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2305.13037v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the fluctuations in equilibrium for a dynamics of rods with random length. This includes the classical hard rod elastic collisions, when rod lengths are constant and equal to a positive value. We prove that in the diffusive space-time scaling, an initial fluctuation of density of particles of velocity $v$, after recentering on its Euler evolution, evolve randomly shifted by a Brownian motion of variance $\mathcal D(v)$.
item.dc:creator: Pablo A. Ferrari, Stefano Olla

item.title: Zero-divisor algebras of graph functions: quantum caging, entangling routing and stochastic first-passage exclusion
item.description: arXiv:2311.11978v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show how algebraic constraints on weighted graphs yield exact localization and controlled transport in quantum and stochastic systems. Antisymmetrizing a noncommutative, nonassociative product of vertex functions defines a Lie bracket. For a specified Lie cobracket over commutative rings without nonzero $2$-torsion, compatibility holds if and only if products of distinct incident edge weights vanish. When the coefficient ring is a finite product of integral domains, the edges with nonzero weights in each component of the ring form a matching. These matchings are determined by the edge weights and need not coincide across the components. These matchings yield exact two-vertex caging in fixed quantum channels; separately specified channel-selective controls enable coherent routing and path--internal-state entanglement. For matching-supported stochastic jump rates, they enforce first-passage exclusion, while prescribed internal-state switching opens inaccessible paths and yields a singular weak-switching escape limit. The bracket--cobracket factorization identifies a common edge operator underlying quantum kinetic Hamiltonians and Markov generators, subject to distinct sign and positivity conditions. The algebra fixes the channel structure; controlled motion requires additional dynamical operations.
item.dc:creator: F\"ul\"op Bazs\'o

item.title: Optimizing the ground state energy of the three-dimensional magnetic Dirichlet Laplacian with constant magnetic field
item.description: arXiv:2504.21597v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper concerns the shape optimization problem of minimizing the ground state energy of the magnetic Dirichlet Laplacian with constant magnetic field among three-dimensional domains of fixed volume. In contrast to the two-dimensional case, a generalized "magnetic" Faber-Krahn inequality does not hold and minimizers cannot be balls when the magnetic field is turned on. An analysis of the problem among cylindrical domains reveals geometric constraints for general minimizers. In particular, minimizers must elongate with a certain rate along the direction of the magnetic field as the field strength increases. In addition to the theoretical analysis, we present numerical minimizers which confirm this prediction and give rise to further conjectures.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Baur

item.title: The Huang-Yang conjecture for the low-density Fermi gas
item.description: arXiv:2505.22340v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Our work establishes a three-term asymptotic expansion of the ground state energy of a dilute gas of spin $1/2$ fermions with repulsive short-range interactions, validating a formula predicted by Huang and Yang in 1957. The formula is universal in the sense that it holds for a large class of interaction potentials and depends on those only via their scattering length. We have recently proved an upper bound on the ground state energy of the desired form, and the present work completes the program by proving the matching lower bound.
item.dc:creator: Emanuela L. Giacomelli, Christian Hainzl, Phan Th\`anh Nam, Robert Seiringer

item.title: Generalised Langevin Dynamics: Significance and Limitations of the Projection Operator Formalism
item.description: arXiv:2604.20453v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We discuss some mathematical aspects of the Mori-Zwanzig projection operator formalism. The core of the Mori-Zwanzig formalism is the generalised Langevin equation, which is typically derived from the Dyson-Duhamel identity. We recall the derivation of the projection operator formalism for Mori's projection by means of semigroup theory, and we discuss where rigorous methods fail for the case of Zwanzig's projection. For bounded perturbations of the time-evolution operator (e.g. for Mori's projection), the Dyson-Duhamel identity coincides with the variation of constants formula. For unbounded perturbations (e.g. for Zwanzigs's projection), the Dyson-Duhamel identity should be considered an equation for the orthogonal dynamics, for which the existence of unique solutions has yet to be established. Then we recall that all properties of Mori's generalised Langevin equation follow directly from the well-posedness of Volterra equations, irrespective of the projection operator formalism. Further, we discuss the use of Mori's generalised Langevin equation as a coarse-grained model. Finally, we illustrate that the memory term is a coupling term that is not necessarily related to memory. To this end, we introduce projections onto subspaces of 'fast' and 'slow' variables that are associated with the spectral decomposition of skew-adjoint operators. For these projections, the memory term vanishes.
item.dc:creator: Christoph Widder, Tanja Schilling

item.title: Homotopies in Batalin-Vilkovisky Formalism
item.description: arXiv:2606.30965v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We review the notion of homotopy of quantum master actions in geometric Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism. Then we construct new examples of such homotopies, coming from renormalization group flow and non-infinitesimal changes of gauge fixing. Finally, we use the field redefinitions given by these homotopies to construct spans of quantum master actions with isomorphic effective actions.
item.dc:creator: Branislav Jur\v{c}o, J\'an Pulmann, Martin Zika

item.title: Recurrence Coefficients of Oscillatory Gegenbauer-type Orthogonal Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2607.19797v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study two classes of oscillatory Gegenbauer-type weight functions. One is $w_1(x)=(1-x^2)^{\lambda-1/2}\exp(i\zeta x),x\in[-1,1]$, where $\lambda>-1/2$ is rational and $\zeta\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$ is a zero of the Bessel function $J_{\lambda-1}$. The other is $w_2(x)=x(1-x^{2})^{\gamma-1/2} \exp(\mathit{i}\eta x), x\in[-1,1]$, where $\gamma$ and $\eta$ are chosen such that the corresponding orthogonal polynomials exist. By using the ladder operators established in recent work for monic orthogonal polynomials associated with Jacobi-type weight functions and three compatibility conditions, we derive two coupled difference equations for the three-term recurrence coefficients corresponding to $w_1$ and $w_2$, respectively. For $w_1$, and for $w_2$ where $\gamma=0$ and $\eta$ is a positive zero of $J_0$, or $\gamma=1/2$ and $\eta=m\pi$ with $m$ denoting a nonzero integer, we determine the initial values for the recurrence coefficients and compute the first few terms via the difference equations. Then we conjecture general-$n$ symbolic forms for the recurrence coefficients and for $\textbf{p}(n)$, the coefficient of $x^{n-1}$ in the monic orthogonal polynomial of degree $n$. The case $\lambda=0$ in $w_1$ is treated separately, since the conjectured general-$\lambda$ forms degenerate here, yielding substantially different results. For $w_1$, we also derive a third-order difference equation satisfied by $\textbf{p}(n)$.
item.dc:creator: Shulin Lyu, Xun Zhou

item.title: Continuum Limit for One-Dimensional Moir\'e Relaxation
item.description: arXiv:2609.37943v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish convergence of minimizers for a minimal one dimensional atomic-scale model for relaxation in moir\'e materials to those of a one-dimensional continuum limit functional analogous to those commonly used in practice to model relaxation. The atomic-scale model consists of two periodic chains containing $N$ and $N+1$ atoms per common cell and is exactly moir\'e-periodic at the atomic scale. Its energy combines harmonic nearest-neighbor intralayer interactions with nonlocal interlayer interactions generated by an even $C^2$ pair potential with polynomial decay. The associated continuum energy couples linear elasticity to a periodic misfit potential, obtained by periodizing the pair potential, which penalizes unfavorable local stackings.
item.dc:creator: Hao Lan, Michael Hott, Jeff Calder, Alexander B. Watson

item.title: Quenched Growth of Normal Matrices and Harmonic Measure
item.description: arXiv:2610.03912v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The eigenvalues of a large normal random matrix form a two-dimensional Coulomb gas. At fixed weight, the spectral droplet grows with the matrix rank, and its semiclassical density increment is harmonic measure. We freeze an $N$-eigenvalue configuration and sample $M$ further eigenvalues using the projection onto polynomials of degree less than $N+M$ that vanish at the frozen points. Their conditional law is an exact polynomial ensemble in the potential of the frozen charges. For a regular analytic droplet, we prove that the spatial distribution of the new eigenvalues converges to harmonic measure on the old boundary when $M/\log N\to\infty$ and $M/N\to0$. This convergence holds conditionally on the frozen spectrum, outside a set of frozen configurations whose probability tends to zero. The equilibrium process formed from orthogonal polynomials of degrees $N,\ldots,N+M-1$ has the same limit. An exact finite-rank identity relates polynomial moments of the conditional mean to fluctuations of the frozen spectrum, with a remainder from polynomial modes of degree $N+M$ and above.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Alekseev

item.title: Simplifying 2-Bundle Descriptions of Invariants and Local Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.35669v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A string couples to a 2-form gauge potential whose local descriptions need not fit together as a single global form. Principal 2-bundles provide a geometric description of this gluing. However, we recover surface amplitudes and quantum partition functions, as well as local classical field dynamics, without the 2-bundle formalism. For surface amplitudes, differential characters preserve curvature and flat phases. Ordinary fake-flat crossed-module connections with a fixed flat quotient and a reference lift lead to abelian differential cocycles with local coefficients. In three-dimensional finite gauge theories with cohomological actions, Fourier transformation evaluates the 2-form field sum and gives a sum of ordinary finite-group gauge partition functions. A four-dimensional quadratic example gives a signature response that admits direct cochain evaluation although replacement by an ordinary finite-group gauge theory fails. Established bundle, operator, and module descriptions provide further comparisons for topological and index invariants and twisted-sheaf moduli. For finite-dimensional smoothly separable central crossed modules, an invertible local substitution removes a pure gauge 1-form from invariant classical actions for any adjustment, leaving an ordinary quotient connection and two tensor fields. One of these tensor fields can be separated globally from the remaining lift data after fixing the quotient connection and choosing a smooth bundle splitting. For compact or semisimple quotients, an equivariant splitting makes this separation compatible with the full gauge symmetry without changing the adjustment.
item.dc:creator: Ferreira Bastien

item.title: An Egorov-type Theorem for Analytic Wick Observables in Quantum Field Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.39806v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide an exact Egorov-type formula, given by a convergent expansion in the semi-classical parameter $\varepsilon > 0$, for the propagation of a certain class of analytic Wick observables with super-exponentially decaying coefficients, under the action of a time-dependent quadratic Hamiltonian. This work generalizes a result established by S. Breteaux for polynomial symbols, and includes the spatially cutoff $P(\varphi)_2$ model, as well as a variant of the H\"oegh-Krohn model.
item.dc:creator: Julien Malartre

item.title: Semiclassical Wave Packet Dynamics For Nonlinear Schr\"odinger Equations with Harmonic Potentials
item.description: arXiv:2611.01108v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose an approximate Hamiltonian dynamics for the Gross--Pitaevskii equation $i\hbar\psi_t = -\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta \psi + V(x)\psi + \hbar^2 \lambda |\psi|^2\psi$ with harmonic potential $V(x)$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$. We do this by extending the Gaussian ansatz of Perez-Garcia et al.~(Phys.~Rev.~A 56, 1424 (1997)) to the semiclassical wave packets of Hagedorn. We derive the evolution equations for the wave packets from the Hamiltonian/symplectic perspective, rather than the Lagrangian/variational one taken by Perez-Garcia et al. We first show that these two perspectives yield identical evolution equations in the Gaussian case. We then derive the evolution equations for an arbitrary element of the semiclassical wave packets. Finally, we demonstrate the efficacy of the approximate dynamics with numerical experiments.
item.dc:creator: Jared Smith, Tomoki Ohsawa

item.title: The massive phase of the two-dimensional Heisenberg model is stable under small anisotropy
item.description: arXiv:2611.01532v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Polyakov predicted that the classical Heisenberg model on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ has exponentially decaying correlations at every temperature, and proofs of this have recently been posted. We show that the massive phase survives small anisotropy. For every inverse temperature $\beta$ there is $\delta(\beta)>0$ such that the $S^2$-valued model with couplings $\sum_iJ^i\sigma_x^i\sigma_y^i$ has exponentially decaying spin two-point functions, uniformly in finite subgraphs with free boundary conditions and in edge strengths up to $\beta$, whenever all $|J^i-1|\le\delta(\beta)$. The same holds for aligned single-ion anisotropy and for nearly isotropic $O(n)$ models with $n\ge3$. Consequently, for the easy-plane model with couplings $\sigma^x\sigma^x+\sigma^y\sigma^y+\lambda\sigma^z\sigma^z$, the onset of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless phase, proved by Garban and de Montgolfier for every $\lambda\in(-1,1)$, moves to zero temperature as $\lambda\uparrow1$. These results rest on the annulus crossing bound of Ding, Huang and Yang, used on one finite annulus where the anisotropy is a bounded perturbation, and on a sign-cluster argument with Ginibre's inequality for anisotropic planar energies. Explicit constants of another isotropic proof give decay for $\beta\le c |\log(1-\lambda)|^{1/2}$. For $n\ge4$ and $|J^i-1|\le\delta$ with $\delta$ small, at $\beta\le(1-\varepsilon)|\log\delta|/(2\pi)$ spin one-point functions decay exponentially away from the boundary under every boundary condition, and two-point functions decay, both on the scale $e^{\pi\beta+O(\sqrt{\beta\log\beta})}$. This is the $O(4)$ threshold: for $n=4$ it matches the renormalization-group crossover to leading order; for $n\ge5$ it lies below the prediction. This part is conditional on estimates of a recent manuscript on the $O(4)$ model, which the proof transfers to anisotropic couplings at one scale; only odd observables transfer.
item.dc:creator: Yan Ru Pei

item.title: Rasterization-based discontinuous integration on the GPU
item.description: arXiv:2611.05186v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we propose a method based on rasterization in computer graphics for the integration of discontinuous functions accurately and efficiently on the GPU. The proposed method takes advantage of the massively parallel architecture of GPUs via a modified graphics pipeline, where discontinuities are encoded through geometric primitives and processed in the rasterization stage, and multisample anti-aliasing (MSAA) is used to improve integration accuracy across subdomain interfaces. We present both hardware- and software-based pipelines and compare their performance in terms of accuracy as well as computational effort on modern GPU hardware with adaptive quadrature on the CPU. For the tested hardware, at approximately comparable median relative error, the hardware pipeline is up to around $100\text{x}$ faster than adaptive quadrature, while the single- and double-precision software pipelines achieve up to $840\text{x}$ and $1200\text{x}$ speedups compared to their adaptive quadrature counterparts. We use the finite cell method as model problem, where cutcells represent discontinuous integrands at the interface of the physical and fictitious domains and demonstrate the performance of the proposed method using numerical benchmarks. The end-to-end finite cell solution runtime is reduced by a factor of $8.3$ to $9.5$ in the single-precision pipeline and by a factor of $62$ to $72$ in the double-precision pipeline at the prescribed integration settings. Therefore, results indicate that the rasterization-based integration method is a promising alternative for the accurate and efficient integration of discontinuous functions in demanding applications on the GPU.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Saberi, Muqtasid Tashfin, Andreas Vogel

item.title: On the Hausdorff measure of sets of non-Lyapunov behaviour, and a Jarnik-type theorem for random Schroedinger operators
item.description: arXiv:2112.14662v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the growth of the norms of transfer matrices of ergodic discrete Schr\"odinger operators in one dimension. It is known that the set of energies at which the rate of exponential growth is slower than prescribed by the Lyapunov exponent is residual in the part of the spectrum at which the Lyapunov exponent is positive. On the other hand, this exceptional set is of vanishing Hausdorff measure with respect to any gauge function $\rho(t)$ such that $\rho(t)/t$ is integrable at zero. Here we show that this condition on $\rho(t)$ can not in general be improved: for operators with independent, identically distributed potentials of sufficiently regular distribution, the set of energies at which the rate of exponential growth is arbitrarily slow has infinite Hausdorff measure with respect to any gauge function $\rho(t)$ such that $\rho(t)/t$ is non-increasing and not integrable at zero. The main technical ingredient, possibly of independent interest, is a Jarn\'ik-type theorem describing the Hausdorff measure of the set of real numbers well approximated by the eigenvalues of the Schr\"odinger operator. The proof of this result relies on the theory of Anderson localisation and on the mass transference principle of Beresnevich--Velani.
item.dc:creator: Sasha Sodin

item.title: Parabolic stochastic quantisation of the fractional $\Phi^4_3$ model in the full subcritical regime
item.description: arXiv:2303.18112v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a construction of the measure of the fractional $\Phi^4$ Euclidean quantum field theory on $\mathbb{R}^3$ in the full subcritical regime via parabolic stochastic quantisation. Our approach is based on a truncated flow equation for the effective description of the model at sufficiently small scales and on coercive estimates for the nonlinear stochastic partial differential equation describing the interacting field. The constructed measure is translation invariant, reflection positive, and has quartic exponential tails.
item.dc:creator: Pawe{\l} Duch, Massimiliano Gubinelli, Paolo Rinaldi

item.title: Approximate recoverability and the quantum data processing inequality
item.description: arXiv:2309.02074v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we discuss the quantum data processing inequality and its refinements that are physically meaningful in the context of approximate recoverability. An important conjecture regarding this due to Seshadreesan et. al. in J. Phys. A: Math. Theor. 48 (2015) is disproved. We prove some inequalities capturing universal approximate recoverability with the Petz recovery map for the sandwiched quasi and R\'enyi relative entropies for the parameter $t=2$. We also obtain convexity theorems on some parametrized versions of the relative entropy and fidelity, which can be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Saptak Bhattacharya

item.title: A Jordan Algebraic Approach to the Landau Problem with a Non-commutative Parameter: From Non-commutativity to Non-associativity
item.description: arXiv:2312.12047v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Non-associative structures arise naturally in several areas of fundamental physics, including the quantum mechanics of charged particles in magnetic monopole backgrounds, or non-geometric flux compactifications in string theory. A key observation motivating the present work is that the non-commutativity of spatial coordinates can be recast as the non-associativity of observables within a Jordan algebraic framework. This paper provides a comprehensive review of the Jordan algebraic, non-associative formulation of quantum mechanics and demonstrates this passage from non-commutativity to non-associativity concretely through the non-commutative Landau problem coupled to a harmonic potential. We begin with a self-contained account of the operator algebra background, covering $C^*$-algebras, von Neumann algebras, and Jordan--Banach ($JB$) and Jordan--von Neumann ($JBW$) algebras, and present the axiomatic formulation of quantum mechanics in terms of the Jordan algebra of observables. We then develop an alternative Hilbert space construction based on 3-cyclic traces, extending the work of Schupp and Szabo to infinite dimensional Jordan algebras. A central result of this work is that the non-commutative parameter $\theta$ can be expressed entirely in terms of an associator in the Jordan algebraic setting. Pure product states and density matrices arising from this construction are characterized within the JBW-algebra framework. A key advantage of our approach is the \emph{explicit} construction of split operators for the non-commutative Landau Hamiltonian, turning an abstract existence result into a concrete decomposition. This leads to the Jordan--Schr\"odinger time-evolution equation for state vectors, whose exact closed-form solution is presented.
item.dc:creator: Tekin Dereli, Ekin S{\i}la Y\"or\"uk

item.title: Symmetries, correlation functions, and entanglement of general quantum Motzkin spin-chains
item.description: arXiv:2408.16070v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Motzkin spin-chains, which include `colorless' (integer spin $s=1$) and `colorful' ($s \geq 2$) variants, are one-dimensional (1D) local integer spin models notable for their lack of a conformal field theory (CFT) description of their low-energy physics, despite being gapless. The colorful variants are particularly unusual, as they exhibit power-law violation of the area-law of entanglement entropy (as $\sqrt{n}$ in system size $n$), rather than a logarithmic violation as seen in a CFT. In this work, we analytically discover several unique properties of these models, potentially suggesting a new universality class for their low-energy physics. We identify a complex structure of symmetries and unexpected scaling behavior in spin-spin correlations, which deviate from known 1D universality classes. Specifically, the $s=1$ chain exhibits $U(1)$ spontaneous symmetry breaking and ferromagnetic order. Meanwhile, the $s \geq 2$ chains do not appear to spontaneously break any symmetries, but display quasi-long-range algebraic order with power-law decaying correlations, inconsistent with standard Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) critical exponents. We also derive asymptotic scaling expressions, with explicit additive constants, for entanglement measures in both colorless and colorful chains, generalizing previous results of Movassagh [J. Math Phys. (2017)], while providing benchmarks for potential quantum simulation experiments. The $\sqrt{n}$ entanglement scaling implies that any matrix-product-state description of these ground states requires bond dimension $e^{\Omega(\sqrt{n})}$; this superpolynomial cost of the standard 1D tensor-network toolkit, along with the analytical tractability of their ground state properties, positions Motzkin spin chains as intriguing testbeds for quantum simulation of many-body physics.
item.dc:creator: Varun Menon, Andi Gu, Ramis Movassagh

item.title: Discontinuous transition in 2D Potts: I. Order-Disorder Interface convergence
item.description: arXiv:2502.04129v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a $q$-state Potts model on the square grid when $q>4$ at the point $T_c(q)$ of its (discontinous) transition. This model exhibits exactly $q+1$ extremal Gibbs measures: $q$ ordered (monochromatic) and one disordered (free). The current work deals with the Dobrushin order--disorder boundary conditions on a finite $N\times N$ box. Our main result is that this interface is a well-defined object, has $\sqrt{N}$ fluctuations, and converges to a Brownian bridge under diffusive scaling. The same holds also for the corresponding FK-percolation model for all $q>4$. Our proofs rely on a coupling between FK-percolation, the six-vertex model, and the random-cluster representation of an Ashkin--Teller model (ATRC), and on a detailed study of the latter. The coupling relates the interface in FK-percolation to a long subcritical cluster in the ATRC model. For this cluster we develop a ``renewal picture'' \`a la Ornstein-Zernike. This is based on fine mixing properties of the ATRC model that we establish using the link to the six-vertex model and its height function. Along the way, we derive various properties of the Ashkin-Teller model, such as Ornstein-Zernike asymptotics for its two-point function. In a companion work, we provide a detailed study of the Potts model under order-order Dobrushin conditions. We show emergence of a free layer of width $\sqrt{N}$ between the two ordered phases (wetting) and establish convergence of its boundaries to two Brownian bridges conditioned not to intersect.
item.dc:creator: Moritz Dober, Alexander Glazman, S\'ebastien Ott

item.title: An Infinite Two-Parameter Family of Octagonal Tilings
item.description: arXiv:2502.04133v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct an infinite two-parameter family of substitution rules with inflation factors $\delta_{(m,n)}=m+n(1+\sqrt{2})$ for integers $m\geq0$ and $n\geq1$, excluding pairs in which $m$ is even and $n$ is odd. Extending four examples from our previous work, we show that each substitution admits a tiling with $8$-fold rotational symmetry and that the associated tilings are repetitive and have finite local complexity. We also classify the inflation factors according to their PV and unimodular properties and illustrate selected cases through perpendicular-space projections and Fourier spectra.
item.dc:creator: April Lynne D. Say-awen, Sam Coates

item.title: Higher operator product expansions in twisted non-Lorentzian field theories
item.description: arXiv:2502.05077v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Twisting theories with super-Poincar\'e symmetry yields topological-holomorphic field theories, whose operator product expansions of local operators can have as coefficients not only ordinary functions but also `derived' functions with nonzero cohomological degree, described by certain elements of sheaf cohomology. Twisting non-Lorentzian supersymmetric theories yields richer phenomena, where topological and holomorphic spacetime coordinates coexist with ordinary (that is, neither topological nor holomorphic) spacetime coordinates. We propose a sheaf-cohomological description of such OPE coefficients for quantum field theories with arbitrary numbers of topological, holomorphic, and/or ordinary spacetime dimensions, and identify necessary and sufficient conditions for the proposed OPE coefficient space to contain nontrivial `derived' functions; in particular, theories with one topological spacetime dimension and multiple ordinary spacetime dimensions provide a smooth analogue of the (holomorphic) raviolo. We then demonstrate that two-point functions in topological twists of free supersymmetric non-Lorentzian field theories appearing in the literature define nontrivial derived functions consistent with our sheaf-theoretic construction.
item.dc:creator: Luigi Alfonsi, Hyungrok Kim

item.title: Integrable self-adaptive moving mesh schemes for multi-component short pulse type equations under periodic and one-end Dirichlet boundary conditions
item.description: arXiv:2507.03880v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we construct integrable self-adaptive moving mesh schemes for multi-component modified short pulse and short pulse equations under periodic and one-end Dirichlet boundary conditions with nonzero boundary values by using the consistency condition with the hodograph transformation. The essential point is that the edge point $x_{0}$ of the hodograph transformation cannot be kept fixed when the boundary value is nonzero. We derive the evolution equation for $x_{0}$ and incorporate it into the semi-discrete moving mesh scheme. Under periodic boundary conditions, the resulting schemes involve an algebraic constraint corresponding to the integral condition of the continuous periodic problem, whereas under one-end Dirichlet boundary conditions they form ordinary differential systems. We also derive multi-soliton solutions in Pfaffian form for the proposed schemes, preserving the integrable structure at the semi-discrete level. Numerical simulations under periodic and one-end Dirichlet boundary conditions demonstrate that the proposed schemes achieve high accuracy even in regions with rapid variation, including the passage of solitons through the computational boundary, and remain stable throughout the simulated time interval.
item.dc:creator: Ayako Hori, Ken-ichi Maruno, Yasuhiro Ohta, Bao-Feng Feng

item.title: Optimal Calibration of Qubit Detuning and Crosstalk
item.description: arXiv:2507.10661v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Characterizing and calibrating physical qubits is essential for maintaining the performance of quantum processors. A key challenge in this process is the presence of crosstalk that complicates the estimation of individual qubit detunings. In this work, we derive optimal strategies for estimating detuning and crosstalk parameters by optimizing Ramsey interference experiments using Fisher information and the Cramer-Rao bound. We compare several calibration protocols, including measurements of a single quadrature at multiple times and of two quadratures at a single time, for a fixed number of total measurements. Our results predict that the latter approach yields the highest precision and robustness in both cases of isolated and coupled qubits. We validate experimentally our approach using a single NV center as well as superconducting transmons. Our approach enables accurate parameter extraction with significantly fewer measurements, resulting in up to a 50% reduction in calibration time while maintaining estimation accuracy.
item.dc:creator: David Shnaiderov, Matan Ben Dov, Yoav Woldiger, Assaf Hamo, Eugene Demler, Emanuele G. Dalla Torre

item.title: The limiting spectral distribution for sparse elliptic random matrices
item.description: arXiv:2508.04891v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper studies sparse elliptic random matrix models which generalize both the classical elliptic ensembles and sparse i.i.d. matrix models by incorporating correlated entries and a tunable sparsity parameter $p_n$. Each $n\times n$ matrix $X_n$ is formed by entry-wise multiplication of an elliptic random matrix by an elliptic matrix of Bernoulli($p_n$) variables, where $np_n$ tends to infinity at a sufficient rate, allowing for interpolation between dense and sparse regimes. The main result establishes that after appropriate normalization, the empirical spectral measures of these matrices converge weakly in probability to the uniform measure on a rotated ellipsoid in the complex plane as the dimension $n$ tends to infinity. Interestingly, the shape of the limiting ellipsoid depends not only on the mirrored entry-wise correlation structure, but also non-trivially on the sparsity limit $p=\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}p_n$.
item.dc:creator: Jackson Carpenter, Sean O'Rourke

item.title: Generalized Fermat's principle and Snell's law for cone structures and applications
item.description: arXiv:2509.26492v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Fermat's principle is fully generalized to the case where a smooth interface separates two cone structures -- Lorentz-Finsler lightcones -- representing wave propagation in a potentially inhomogeneous, anisotropic, time-dependent and discontinuous medium. The interface, wave source and receiver are assumed to be a hypersurface, a submanifold and a curve in the spacetime, respectively, of any causal character. For a trajectory to fulfill Fermat's principle -- i.e., to be a critical point of the arrival time functional -- its direction must change at the interface, obeying a precise condition that generalizes Snell's law of refraction when the wave crosses the interface, or the law of reflection when it remains in a single medium. Both laws are analyzed in detail to establish the conditions ensuring the existence and uniqueness of refracted and reflected trajectories, and to determine whether they actually minimize the arrival time. Applications to Zermelo's navigation problem and the determination of geodesics in discretized spacetimes are also emphasized.
item.dc:creator: Miguel \'Angel Javaloyes, Steen Markvorsen, Enrique Pend\'as-Recondo, Miguel S\'anchez

item.title: Polychromatic Localized Waves with Complex Frequencies in Nonlinear Maxwell Equations with Material Dispersion
item.description: arXiv:2511.21467v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the existence of polychromatic solutions of cubically nonlinear Maxwell equations in the whole space and with dispersive media, i.e., with a time delayed polarization. Due to the complex nature of the dielectric function, the frequencies are complex, resulting in a decay in time. The geometry is that of a waveguide in $x$ with the propagation direction being $y$ and the solutions are localized in $x$ and have a transverse magnetic polarization. These are often referred to as breathers. They are given as a Fourier series in $y$ and $t$ with the leading frequency $\omega$ being an eigenvalue of a corresponding operator pencil on $\mathbb{R}$ (in the $x$ variable). Each term in the series corresponds to a different temporal decay rate or a different frequency. The series is constructed iteratively via a sequence of linear ordinary differential equations. Our general result provides the existence under some assumptions on the spectrum and on estimates of the resolvent of the corresponding linear operator. We also produce an example of a waveguide given by the interface of two spatially homogeneous physically relevant media for which these assumptions are satisfied. For such an interface setting the constructed solutions correspond to nonlinear polychromatic surface plasmons.
item.dc:creator: Tomas Dohnal, Maximilian Hanisch, Runan He

item.title: Nonperturbative Resummation of Divergent Time-Local Generators: Disentangling Non-Markovian Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2603.25512v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Perturbative van Kampen cumulant expansions of time-local generators of open quantum systems generically diverge at long times, while the reduced dynamics remains regular. We show that these divergences encode information sufficient to reconstruct an approximate nonperturbative dynamical map. Although their resummation remains divergent, disentangling the dynamics according to its van Hove limit resolves the divergence and exposes its dynamical origin: the map approaches isolated times at which it becomes noninvertible. For the weak-coupling unbiased spin--boson model, the reconstructed non-Markovian dynamics takes the disentangled form \begin{equation*} \Phi=\Phi_{\mathrm{GAD}}+\Phi_{\mathrm{NS}}+\Phi_{\mathrm{Khal}}, \end{equation*} separating generalized amplitude damping, exponentially damped nonsecular coherence mixing, and a projective, phase-selective Khalfin map. Thus, the onset of recurrent noninvertibility is the reduced-dynamical-map manifestation of the Khalfin transition from exponential to algebraic relaxation. Although the coherences acquire algebraic Khalfin tails, the distinguishability of quantum superposition states remains governed by an exponential decay law well after the Khalfin transition. Comparison with numerically exact TEMPO dynamics validates the procedure and shows that apparently complex non-Markovian dynamics can resolve into a small number of distinct, physically transparent dynamical processes.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Davidovic 2026 J. Phys. A: Math. Theor.
item.dc:creator: Dragomir Davidovic

item.title: How acausal equations emerge from causal dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2604.07031v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a causal and covariantly stable kinetic model whose spectrum at real wavenumbers $k$ reproduces any rest-frame stable dissipative dispersion relation $\omega(k)$ via suitable initialization of the microscopic degrees of freedom. Macroscopic observables can therefore obey arbitrary linear evolution equations (including forms that would be acausal if taken as fundamental), while the underlying dynamics remains causal, and all apparent propagation is encoded in the initial data. This provides an explicit counterexample to the idea that microscopic causality alone constrains the analytic form of dispersion relations at real $k$. In particular, bounds on transport coefficients based solely on the analytic structure of $\omega(k)$, such as the hydrohedron bounds, require additional assumptions about the region in the complex $k$-plane where $\omega(k)$ corresponds to physical modes.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Gavassino

item.title: Discontinuous transition in 2D Potts: II. Wetting and Brownian watermelon
item.description: arXiv:2604.21669v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The $q$-state Potts model is an archetypical model for various types of phase transitions. We consider it on the square grid and focus on the regime where it undergoes a discontinuous transition, that is $q>4$. At the transition point $T_c(q)$, there are exactly $q+1$ extremal Gibbs measures (pure phases): $q$ ordered (monochromatic) and one disordered (free). This work establishes for the first time the wetting phenomenon in a precise geometric form and in the entire regime of discontinuity $q>4$: at $T_c(q)$, between two ordered phases a disordered layer emerges and, in the diffusive scaling, its boundaries converge to a pair of Brownian motions conditioned not to intersect. This is starkly different from the subcritical ($T<T_c(q)$) behaviour. At $T_c(q)$, previous results (Bricmont--Lebowitz '87, Messager--Miracle-Sole--Ruiz--Shlosman '91) were limited to the construction and properties of the surface tension for large enough $q$. In a companion work, arXiv:2502.04129, we provide a detailed study of the Potts model under order-disorder Dobrushin conditions. That work also develops a ``renewal picture'' \`a la Ornstein-Zernike for a suitable percolation model, which plays a central part in our study of the Potts interfaces. The latter is the random-cluster representation of an Ashkin--Teller model (ATRC), and is related to the Potts model via a chain of couplings going through the six-vertex model. In the current work, we extend the analysis to a pair of interacting order-disorder interfaces forming the separation between the two ordered phases, and couple them to a pair of well-behaved random walks conditioned not to intersect. The construction of the coupling is based on rigorously deriving entropic repulsion between the two interfaces. We also prove convergence of interfaces in the FK-percolation model at $p_c(q)$ when $q>4$.
item.dc:creator: Moritz Dober, Alexander Glazman, S\'ebastien Ott

item.title: Carrollian quantum states and flat space holography
item.description: arXiv:2604.22745v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study free Carrollian quantum field theories from an algebraic perspective and explore their implications for flat space holography. As explicit examples, we construct the electric and magnetic Carrollian Weyl algebras obtained from Carroll limits of the relativistic scalar field and analyze their states, including vacuum and thermal configurations. For the massive electric theory, we find a regular Carroll-invariant vacuum state and a regular KMS state, yielding a consistent Carrollian thermodynamic system. By contrast, the massless electric and magnetic theories are more subtle: depending on the quantization, they admit either no regular distinguished vacuum or only nonregular Carroll-invariant ground states, while still supporting nonregular thermal states. We further analyze alternative classes of states in the massless electric theory, including spatially homogeneous quasifree pure states and Sorkin--Johnston states. Motivated by these results, we discuss consequences for flat space holography. We construct a well-defined state relevant for Carrollian holography whose Hilbert-space representation factorizes into a standard Fock sector and a nonseparable zero-mode sector, thereby highlighting the role of infrared degrees of freedom in the boundary theory.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Fredenhagen, Stefan Prohazka, Robert Tiefenbacher

item.title: An algebra of proper observables at null infinity: Dirac brackets, Memory and Goldstone probes
item.description: arXiv:2605.13804v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a rigorous evaluation of Dirac brackets for classical observables on the phase space of radiative gravitational modes at null infinity that naturally incorporates memory effects. Considering the Ashtekar-Streubel phase space, with boundary conditions in time given by vanishing {\it news} and purely electric {\it shear}, and taking into account the infinite dimensionality of the phase space, we identify the algebra of proper observables (understood as functions on phase space that can be associated with smooth symplectic flows). We show that the action of supertranslation charges generate the correct transformations on the shear. We also show that the conventional definition of the ``Goldstone mode'' adopted in the literature cannot be associated with a proper observable, but nevertheless there exists an infinite family of proper observables, which we call {\it Goldstone probes}, that are capable of measuring the Goldstone mode. We notice that there are no Goldstone probes constructed only out of the shear {\it or} the news, providing a possible explanation for why attempts to construct a (separable) Hilbert space with different memory states have failed so far. Finally, we derive formulas for distributional Dirac brackets between local shear and news, and show that they contain non-local corrections.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Andrade e Silva, Simone Speziale

item.title: Repeated differentiation of deterministic polynomials with asymptotically radial root distributions
item.description: arXiv:2607.16954v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent works of Galligo, Najnudel, and Vu (2025) and Najnudel and Vu (2026) study repeated differentiation for polynomials of the form $P(z)=p(z^m)$, where $p$ is a deterministic polynomial of degree $n$ with real, non-negative roots, in the regime where $m$ and $n$ are large. If $m\gg \log(n)$ and the root distribution of $P$ converges to a compactly supported, radial probability measure $\mu_0$, these works show that for $0\le t<1$, the root distribution of the $\lfloor nmt\rfloor$-th derivative of $P$ converges to a compactly supported probability measure $\mu_t$ given by an explicit formula for its radial quantile function. We give a substantially simplified proof of this result and also extend the result from repeated differentiation to repeated applications of the differential operator $z^a(d/dz)^b$. Our proof is based on new, sharp estimates on the roots of polynomial with real, non-negative roots in terms of the coefficients of the polynomial. We also compute the limiting root distribution in the case when $m$ is fixed and $n$ tends to infinity. Then letting $m$ tend to infinity we obtain the same limit as before. Along the way, we prove a generalization of the free multiplicative law of large numbers that is of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Brian C. Hall, Daniel Perales

item.title: The D'Alembert-Lagrange Principle and Lagrange Equations
item.description: arXiv:2607.24825v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this expository-research article we present a rigorous geometric framework for analytical mechanics in the extended phase space, accommodating general constraints that may be non-linear in velocities. We prove that the space of virtual displacements and ideal constraint reactions depend strictly on the intrinsic geometry of the constraint manifold and are entirely invariant under the choice of analytical constraint equations. Furthermore, we show that the Lagrange equations of the second kind are derived through the covector covariance of the variational derivative operator under the embedding mapping of the configuration manifold.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Zubelevich

item.title: How much averaged null energy must an anisotropic bounce violate?
item.description: arXiv:2608.29556v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that in Einstein gravity a null-complete, non-static Bianchi I universe (homogeneous, spatially flat and anisotropic) violates the averaged null energy condition (ANEC) along every complete light ray outside at most four null directions, and along all of them if its total energy density, cosmological constant included, is ever positive. Along each complete ray the averaged null energy is at most $-J_p/(8\pi G)$, with equality whenever the integral converges, where $J_p$ is the squared expansion and shear accumulated by a thin bundle of light rays. With spatial sections $\mathbb{R}^3$ the achronal ANEC therefore leaves only Minkowski space, as for flat and open Friedmann models. Under the pointwise null energy condition, every null geodesic of a non-static Bianchi I universe is incomplete. The isotropic bounce of effective loop quantum cosmology has $J_p=1.478\,\omega_B H_{\max}$ (light frequency at the bounce times largest Hubble rate), and at the same critical density the cheapest ray of a strongly anisotropic bounce pays four to five times as much. A Casimir-supported turning point on a three-torus has a deficit of the same order, but at Hubble rates well below the Planck scale its light rays circumnavigate the torus and are not achronal, so the achronal ANEC does not apply to them.
item.dc:creator: Alan Zhang, Ye Zhou

item.title: Alternative Boundary Conditions in Asymptotically Anti-de Sitter Spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2609.10805v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetimes are not globally hyperbolic, so boundary conditions are generally needed for well-defined dynamics. Ishibashi and Wald (IW) determined boundary conditions yielding well-posed dynamics with conserved positive energy for scalar, electromagnetic, and linearized gravitational fields, using nonlocal potentials and individual spherical harmonic modes. In this paper, we determine which IW conditions are local in the primary fields and which are AdS-invariant. In four spacetime dimensions, the standard AdS-invariant boundary conditions set the rescaled magnetic field to zero for electromagnetism and the rescaled magnetic Weyl tensor to zero for Einstein gravity on the conformal boundary. We generalize these standard boundary conditions by setting arbitrary linear combinations of the electric and magnetic fields, or the corresponding Weyl tensors, to zero, and we conjecture that these exhaust the local, AdS-invariant, conservative boundary conditions in AdS$_{1,3}$. Boundary conditions with non-AdS-invariance and in different spacetime dimensions are also studied. The AdS-invariant conditions in AdS$_{1,3}$ extend to Yang-Mills theory and nonlinear gravity in a general Fefferman-Graham setting. We construct phase spaces for these general boundary conditions. The covariant phase spaces for general conditions are naturally associated with Lagrangians containing Pontryagin terms and, in gravity, a Gauss-Bonnet term. In gravity, except for the standard boundary condition, no nontrivial asymptotic symmetries exist and all conserved charges such as ADM mass vanish identically, as in a closed universe. Spacetimes with Killing fields including AdS then exhibit linearization instability in the sense of Fischer and Marsden and Moncrief. For nonstandard boundary conditions, the modified symplectic structure yields new expressions for the entropy formula of black holes.
item.dc:creator: Robert M. Wald, Xinkang Wang

item.title: A complete classification of the existence of finite-dimensional quantum solutions to inconsistent linear constraint systems
item.description: arXiv:2609.16490v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Linear constraint systems (LCS) provide a compact algebraic language for nonlocal games and state-independent contextuality. In the binary case the Mermin--Peres square shows that inconsistent LCS can be solved by promoting variables to local Pauli operators, whereas a series of no-go results excludes analogous Pauli-, Clifford- and monomial unitary-based constructions at odd prime modulus. We first isolate the reason for this difference: for tensor-product quantum solutions, the obstruction to a classical solution of a LCS over $\mathbb{Z}_n$ decomposes into obstruction classes carried by the individual factors. As a consequence, a genuinely global obstruction cannot arise solely by tensoring locally unobstructed systems. The argument is specific to odd modulus; at even modulus the reordering phase need not vanish, as in Pauli-based examples. Given this distinction, we instead associate LCS to finite arrangements of rank-one projectors and resolutions of the identity in finite-dimensional vector spaces. Quantum solvability for such LCS is automatic and the search for a quantum-classical gap rests entirely on proving classical unsatisfiability of the underlying modular incidence problem of the arrangement. By relating such LCS with group-valued frame functions, we identify a family of examples in the work of [Harding, Jager, and Smith, Int. J. Theor. Phys. 44, 539 (2005)]. To establish the (non)existence of classically unsatisfiable LCS over $\mathbb{Z}_n$ with quantum solutions in all dimensions $d$ and for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$, we further construct explicit examples for the cases $d=n$ prime. Our main result thus positively resolves the existence problem of such LCS beyond the binary case: such systems exist if and only if $d\geq 3$ and $\gcd(n,d)>1$. Moreover, we establish the existence of LCS with a quantum-classical gap over finite fields if and only if $d\geq 3$ and $p\mid d$.
item.dc:creator: Markus Frembs

item.title: Revisiting the Frolov--Zelnikov solution for Majumdar--Papapetrou black holes
item.description: arXiv:2609.23921v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We revisit Frolov and Zelnikov's electrostatic Green function for a test charge in a multi-center Majumdar--Papapetrou spacetime, correcting its horizon-charge condition and extending the result to higher dimensions. In four dimensions, we derive the exact Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for a minimally coupled spectator Maxwell field with independently prescribed horizon potentials. The horizon flux charges obey a capacitance matrix with entries $C_{AA}=M_A+\sum_{B\ne A}M_AM_B/R_{AB}$ and $C_{AB}=-M_AM_B/R_{AB}$, where $M_A$ are center masses and $R_{AB}$ their separations. This matrix is a positive diagonal term plus a weighted graph Laplacian, yielding an exact common-mode/differential-mode decomposition of the field energy. The grounded Dirichlet Green function partitions a point charge's flux among infinity and the horizons through harmonic measures. We show that the diagonal condition imposed by Frolov and Zelnikov [Eq.~(4.14)] preserves only the total horizon charge, allowing redistribution between individual horizons. A corrected symmetric Green function preserving each horizon charge instead involves the inverse capacitance matrix. For two centers, the correction produces a finite, negative-semidefinite self-energy shift and an exact self-force difference, without additional ultraviolet subtraction. Finally, we extend the capacitance matrix, flux partition, and fixed-charge Green function to $D=n+3$ dimensions, where the graph weights contain the universal factor $\pi^{n/2}/\Gamma(n/2)$.
item.dc:creator: Jongheon Baek, Gihwan Nam

item.title: Upper deviations of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick free energy: the fifth-order law and the onset of constrained Parisi measures
